selection: EU banking digital sovereignty market gap
description: Whether a market gap exists for an EU retail bank marketing digital/European sovereignty as its central value proposition. Captures the demand-side figures that are measurable, the layers where sovereignty is actually marketed, the sovereignty-washing risk, and the central negative finding (no such retail bank observed via web search up to 2026-07-01). Numeric confidence is not a schema field; epistemic limits are carried in the word and source descriptions instead.

words.name: sovereignty bank
words.description: a hypothetical EU retail bank whose central value proposition is digital/European sovereignty; the subject of this Fermi estimate. Not an observed real entity.

triples.name: digital sovereignty
triples.description: the capacity to retain full control over data, systems and technological decisions, free from external legal or political coercion; requires that ownership, operation and legal domicile all lie within the intended jurisdiction, so data residency alone is insufficient.

triples.name: European sovereignty
triples.description: digital sovereignty specifically vested in European ownership, operation and jurisdiction.

triples.name: governance sovereignty
triples.description: axis of the two-axis zukunft.com sovereignty model: the degree to which ownership structure, operational control and legal jurisdiction of a provider lie outside foreign (especially US) reach.

triples.name: license sovereignty
triples.description: axis of the two-axis zukunft.com sovereignty model: the degree to which the technology stack is open-source or otherwise free from proprietary foreign control.

triples.name: sovereignty washing
triples.description: marketing a product as digitally sovereign while it remains structurally and legally subject to a foreign jurisdiction; arises whenever the parent company is US-domiciled, so the US CLOUD Act conflict with EU data-protection law is unresolved regardless of EU data-centre location.

triples.name: EU retail bank
triples.description: a licensed deposit-taking bank offering accounts and payment services to private end customers within the EU; distinguished from central banks, payment initiatives and B2B banking-software or cloud providers.

triples.name: card payment
triples.description: a payment made using a debit or credit card.

triples.name: card payment in the euro area
triples.description: card payments processed for transactions within the euro area.

triples.name: US payment provider
triples.description: a payment-service provider domiciled in the United States (for example the large international card networks).

triples.name: share of US payment providers
triples.description: the fraction of card payments in the euro area processed by US-domiciled payment providers.

triples.name: regional provider
triples.description: a local or regional technology provider, as opposed to a global hyperscaler.

triples.name: geopolitical intent to use regional providers
triples.description: buyer-survey intent to increase use of local or regional providers for geopolitical reasons; Gartner labels the underlying trend geopatriation.

triples.name: digital euro launch
triples.description: the earliest expected introduction year of the digital euro.

triples.name: EU retail bank sovereignty market gap
triples.description: the conjectured unmet market segment for an EU retail bank whose central value proposition is digital/European sovereignty; no such bank was observed via web search up to 2026-07-01, but a negative web-search finding cannot be proven exhaustive, so this is tagged as an assumed value.

triples.name: sovereignty washing enabled by US CLOUD Act
triples.description: sovereignty washing is enabled where the US CLOUD Act (with FISA 702) lets US authorities reach data held by US-parented providers regardless of EU server location.

triples.name: privacy concern
triples.description: a consumer's concern about the privacy of their digital payments or banking activity; measured by ECB SPACE 2024 at 60% of euro-area consumers.

triples.name: account holder
triples.description: a consumer holding a payment account.

triples.name: privacy-concerned account holder
triples.description: an account holder who reports privacy concern; the top of the addressable funnel for a sovereignty bank.

triples.name: switching willingness
triples.description: the share of privacy-concerned holders who would actually switch bank AND pay for a sovereignty offering. Deliberately discounted hard to reflect the attitude-behavior gap: stating a survey concern is not revealed willingness to switch a sticky primary bank and pay a fee.

triples.name: captured market share
triples.description: the share of the switch-willing pool a single new entrant realistically wins over several years, given competition, trust-building and incumbent stickiness.

triples.name: sovereignty bank customer
triples.description: a paying customer of the hypothetical sovereignty bank; the result of applying switching willingness and captured share to the privacy-concerned pool.

triples.name: contribution margin per customer
triples.description: annual contribution margin per paying customer in EUR, net of cost to serve; assumes a fee-based model with no data monetization and no interchange-heavy card economics.

triples.name: sovereignty bank annual profit
triples.description: the estimated possible annual profit of the hypothetical sovereignty bank; the terminal node of the Fermi chain. Range spans more than two orders of magnitude because three independently uncertain discount factors multiply.

sources.name: Bundesbank digital euro sovereignty
sources.description: Deutsche Bundesbank, speech and topic page by President Nagel on the digital euro and European sovereignty, 2026. Institutional source; the underlying ECB figure was not independently verified against the primary ECB study.

sources.name: Gartner geopatriation via bancos
sources.description: Gartner Cloud Buying Behavior Survey 2025 figure, cited secondarily by bancos.com (2026). Secondary source; the primary Gartner survey was not verified.

sources.name: digitalbusiness sovereignty washing
sources.description: digitalbusiness-magazin.de (2026), analysis of sovereignty washing and the conflict between EU data-protection law and the US CLOUD Act and FISA 702.

sources.name: zukunft.com market-gap analysis
sources.description: zukunft.com analysis, 2026-07-01. The market-absence finding is a negative result from web search and is intrinsically not exhaustively provable; recorded as an assumed value.

sources.name: ECB SPACE 2024
sources.description: ECB, Study on the payment attitudes of consumers in the euro area (SPACE) 2024. Primary source. 60% of euro-area consumers concerned about privacy in digital payments; payment-account holding at 93%.

formulas.name: sovereignty bank profit (formula)
formulas.expression: "sovereignty bank annual profit" = "privacy-concerned account holder" * "switching willingness" * "captured market share" * "contribution margin per customer"

formulas.name: sovereignty bank customer count (formula)
formulas.expression: "sovereignty bank customer" = "privacy-concerned account holder" * "switching willingness" * "captured market share"

calc-validation.note: base case: 165,000,000 * 0.02 * 0.05 * 45. Percent values scale as fractions.
